note: Product findings exposed by the real-input golden-path journeys. None is repaired by PR-TEST-DESKTOP-830; the harness records the workaround it needed for each so a green journey is never read as defect-free. Evidence sources are exploratory runs made on the pre-commit tree (base 7f381e2c) and are preserved into the acceptance baseline with their SHA-256.

findings.title: Learning Rate step collapses the 1-5 Rating box after the first saved rating

environment.window: application default (about 1916x1040); reproduced at window heights of 1040 px or less

reproduction: Open the Learning tab and run a designed experiment with at least two variants.
Open the Rate step and save the first rating.
Look for the 1-5 Rating box for the next variant.
findings.expected: The Rating controls, the selected variant information and Save Rating / Save & Next stay reachable.
findings.observed: The Recommendations box takes the height of the Rating box, which is squeezed to zero height; the controls cannot be clicked. Re-confirmed by the PR-830 amendment acceptance run at the application's normal (non-maximized) startup size: LRN-01 is BLOCKED at the rating control (ControlUnreachable: rating 4, hidden).
findings.harness_workaround: The window is maximized and the workspace divider is dragged before rating (recorded as window_forced_maximized and pane_dragged_to_reveal_controls).

evidence.description: Failure screenshot of the Rate step with the Rating box absent
Same failure, second reproduction
Acceptance run, layout normal (no maximize): LRN-01 failure screenshot

repair.summary: The Learning review panel's side column scrolls as one body (sections keep natural height, a taller pane still stretches the Rating row) above a fixed Save strip; a scroll box at its limit hands the wheel to the page around it.
repair.verification: Windows-driver journeys IMG-01, VID-01 and LRN-01 at the normal, 1280x680 minimum and maximized layouts: normal 20261104T162625Z_simulated_a18c7403_normal_acceptance_78bb76, minimum 20261104T163042Z_simulated_a18c7403_minimum_acceptance_f052d4, maximized 20261104T163431Z_simulated_a18c7403_maximized_acceptance_a550d7

findings.title: Focus-induced scrolling moves a pressed control between mouse press and release (every journey, every layout)
findings.area: Pack list Refresh, Model combobox, Learning source combobox
reproduction: Scroll so the control sits near the edge of a scrolling page.
Press the mouse button on the control and release.
The focus-in reveal scrolls the page (up to about 200 px) between press and release.
findings.expected: One ordinary click activates the control.
findings.observed: The control moved under the pointer between press and release; the release landed elsewhere and the click was lost. Measured on the acceptance runs: the release had to follow the control 3 to 8 times per journey in all three layouts, in IMG-01 and VID-01 as well as LRN-01, so it is general rather than limited to the three controls first noticed.
findings.harness_workaround: The driver settles after the press and moves the pointer onto the control before release, and retries clicks that had no effect (recorded as mouse_release_followed_moving_control and click_retried_after_no_effect).

evidence.description: Trace rows with pointer_followed_control in the accepted exploratory run
Acceptance run, layout normal: pointer_followed_control events

repair.summary: The page-wide focus reveal no longer scrolls a control the pointer is already on, so focus gained by a mouse press cannot move the control between press and release; Tab and programmatic focus still reveal.
repair.verification: Windows-driver journeys IMG-01, VID-01 and LRN-01 at the normal, 1280x680 minimum and maximized layouts: normal 20261104T162625Z_simulated_a18c7403_normal_acceptance_78bb76, minimum 20261104T163042Z_simulated_a18c7403_minimum_acceptance_f052d4, maximized 20261104T163431Z_simulated_a18c7403_maximized_acceptance_a550d7

findings.title: Closing during an in-flight LoRA-Discovery scan stalls 10 s and logs an ERROR
reproduction: Start the application and close it while the LoRA-Discovery scan is still running.
findings.expected: Shutdown cancels the worker and completes promptly without errors.
findings.observed: The scan posts a callback to the Tk thread that is joining it; shutdown waits the full 10 s and logs "[thread_registry] Thread 'LoRA-Discovery' did not shutdown within 10.0s timeout!".
findings.harness_workaround: The harness waits up to 20 s for non-daemon threads to settle before closing.

evidence.description: Diagnostics of a run that captured the ERROR

repair.summary: ThreadRegistry.shutdown_all runs registered shutdown listeners before joining; the LoRA discovery scan registers its cancel there, so a close during a scan no longer waits the scan out.
repair.verification: Windows-driver journeys IMG-01, VID-01 and LRN-01 at the normal, 1280x680 minimum and maximized layouts: normal 20261104T162625Z_simulated_a18c7403_normal_acceptance_78bb76, minimum 20261104T163042Z_simulated_a18c7403_minimum_acceptance_f052d4, maximized 20261104T163431Z_simulated_a18c7403_maximized_acceptance_a550d7

findings.title: A pending tooltip timer during teardown re-enters the application's destroy
reproduction: Hover a tooltip-bearing control so a show timer is pending.
Close the window; the timer fires during teardown and its update_idletasks re-enters _destroy_root.
findings.expected: Teardown cancels pending callbacks; no reentrant idle update.
findings.observed: One access-violation crash of the process (faulthandler trace retained); not reliably reproducible.
findings.harness_workaround: The pointer is moved off the controls and the loop pumped before the close command is sent.

evidence.description: faulthandler trace of the crash

repair.summary: Tooltip show/hide are idempotent and tolerate a destroyed widget or popup; the pending timer is cancelled when the widget is destroyed and its id is cleared when it fires.
repair.verification: Windows-driver journeys IMG-01, VID-01 and LRN-01 at the normal, 1280x680 minimum and maximized layouts: normal 20261104T162625Z_simulated_a18c7403_normal_acceptance_78bb76, minimum 20261104T163042Z_simulated_a18c7403_minimum_acceptance_f052d4, maximized 20261104T163431Z_simulated_a18c7403_maximized_acceptance_a550d7

findings.title: Requested window geometry is not honoured at startup
reproduction: Request a window geometry before the application builds its window.
Compare the requested and observed size.
findings.expected: Either the requested size, or a documented saved-state restoration.
findings.harness_workaround: The windows driver maximizes after boot so every run has the same canvas.
findings.classification_open: Not yet distinguished from intentional saved-state restoration or a harness ordering issue; PR-GUI-RELIABILITY-831 must classify it before any repair.

evidence.description: window_1 observation (maximized size) and display facts of the accepted exploratory run

repair.classification: not an operator-visible defect; harness assumption
repair.summary: Reproduced as a mechanism, not as a defect: an unmapped Tk window reports a 1x1 geometry, so the startup policy (saved window state, else the screen-aware default) always applies, and a geometry requested before the application builds its window is overridden. No operator path requests a size before the window exists, and honouring one would change the first-run window size. The harness selects its layout after boot (--layout), which the application does honour.

findings.title: MediaInspector has no attribute _current_path (inherited)
reproduction: Run tests/tools/test_operator_journey_gui.py::test_discovered_outputs_journey_passes_on_an_isolated_output_tree on unchanged main.
findings.expected: The discovered-outputs journey passes on an isolated output tree.
findings.observed: Fails identically on unchanged HEAD with AttributeError: MediaInspector has no attribute '_current_path'. Documented in docs/work_packages/IMG_EVIDENCE_AUTOPILOT_800.md.
findings.harness_workaround: None; the test is reported as a known inherited failure and is not weakened.

evidence.description: Regression run log showing the failure on a clean HEAD worktree

repair.summary: The discovered-outputs journey read a private attribute that MediaInspector no longer has; it now uses the inspector's public current_path(). The test is unchanged.

findings.title: Stale Tk after-callbacks fire after the root is destroyed at shutdown
reproduction: Run any golden-path journey and close the window through the system close command.
Read shutdown_noise_after_close in the journey evidence.
findings.expected: Closing the window cancels every scheduled callback; no Tcl background error is raised afterwards.
findings.observed: Each journey records four tcl-bgerror entries after close: invalid command name "<id>_pump" (three) and "<id>_tick" (one), i.e. scheduled after-callbacks outliving their widgets. Not an application crash and not captured as a GUI error, so journeys still PASS; the noise is retained as evidence and is counted in the comparison's error_count.
findings.harness_workaround: None. The harness records the noise as shutdown_noise_after_close and never filters it.

evidence.description: Acceptance run, layout maximized: shutdown_noise_after_close per journey

repair.summary: The invoker pump and the running-job elapsed timer are cancelled with their widgets, so no after-callback outlives the widget that owns it.
repair.verification: Windows-driver journeys IMG-01, VID-01 and LRN-01 at the normal, 1280x680 minimum and maximized layouts: normal 20261104T162625Z_simulated_a18c7403_normal_acceptance_78bb76, minimum 20261104T163042Z_simulated_a18c7403_minimum_acceptance_f052d4, maximized 20261104T163431Z_simulated_a18c7403_maximized_acceptance_a550d7

findings.title: A job that fails because the checkpoint changed shows only a generic failure; the cause is only in the log
findings.area: Queue and History, failed job detail
reproduction: Queue a job, then change the active WebUI checkpoint outside StableNew before dispatch (OPS-01 case C).
Open the queue or History row of the failed job.
findings.expected: The job's error message or History detail says the checkpoint no longer matches and nothing was generated.
findings.observed: The job fails (correctly: zero generation requests were sent) but its recorded error message and History text carry only a generic message; the checkpoint mismatch is visible only in the application log.
findings.harness_workaround: None. OPS-01 records the check failure failure_cause_visible_to_operator rather than reading the log.

evidence.description: OPS-01 changed-model case: error message, History text and the zero-POST proof

repair.summary: A checkpoint the WebUI will not select now fails the job with a bounded, path-free reason in the canonical error message: it names the requested and reported checkpoints, says no images were generated and says to restore the model or prepare a new job. Backend-unreachable and other failures keep their own messages; zero generation POSTs are sent. The Job History status cell shows the recorded reason as a tooltip.

findings.title: An unreachable backend leaves a job in the running state while the banner reports jobs held
reproduction: Stop the WebUI endpoint, queue one job and let the runner pick it up (OPS-01 case A and the in-flight cases).
Compare the queue row, the job's recorded status and the connectivity banner.
findings.expected: The job's visible state and the banner agree: a job that cannot be dispatched is held (queued), not running.
findings.observed: Observation recorded by OPS-01: while the backend is unreachable the repository status is 'running' although the banner says no jobs are running and the WebUI jobs are held. The job does complete exactly once after the backend returns.
findings.harness_workaround: None. The journey accepts either state while down and asserts exactly-once completion after recovery.

evidence.description: OPS-01 unreachable_before_dispatch outcome (visible banner text and job statuses)

repair.summary: Cause: the job was legitimately claimed (no hold existed) and sat RUNNING in the executor's readiness wait; the Operator Readiness window then showed an older snapshot ('WebUI jobs are held in the queue', 0 held) next to a RUNNING row. The queue projection now counts claimed RUNNING WebUI jobs, the readiness record names them and never says jobs are held in the queue when none is, and the window states when its snapshot was taken. No lifecycle, claim, dispatch-certainty or requeue rule changed. The deeper 'preparing / waiting for the backend' state is GP833-F1 (owner decision).

findings.title: A masked edit started from History does not record its parent job, so Compare with Parent is unavailable for it
findings.area: History Iterate, Review Edit Mask, History Compare with Parent
reproduction: Complete a txt2img job and select it in History.
Iterate... then Edit Image in Review, then Edit Mask..., paint a region, enter an edit prompt, Preview frozen job and Add prepared job to Queue.
Select the finished edit job in History.
findings.expected: The edit's frozen source carries parent_job_id (the History job it was iterated from), and Compare with Parent is offered and shows parent and edit.
findings.observed: The edit NJR source records parent_artifact_id (the source image digest) but parent_job_id is null, so has_recorded_parent is false and Compare with Parent is disabled. The History hand-off does carry source_job_id, but MaskEditorDialog is opened with only the image path and takes parent_job_id from the image's embedded metadata, which has no job id.
findings.harness_workaround: None: IMG-03 keeps parent_job_recorded and compare_offered_for_the_edit as failing checks and does not queue a different edit path to obtain a parent.

evidence.description: IMG-03 edit_lineage_fields observation and the two failing checks

repair.summary: The History hand-off's source job identity is carried from Review into the Edit Mask and Extend Canvas dialogs and bound to the loaded bytes (recorded path, source artifact digest, embedded job id) before it becomes the frozen source's parent_job_id. A different image, changed bytes or a contradicting claim are refused; an image with no hand-off keeps no parent.

findings.title: Sequence admission requires the form-level motion prompt even when every shot has its own prompt
reproduction: Select a prompt-directed workflow and a source image, author three shots each with a motion prompt, leave the form's own Motion prompt empty.
Queue Sequence.
findings.expected: Queue Sequence is admitted, or the refusal explains that the form prompt is also required and why.
findings.observed: Not queued: the workflow 'needs a prompt describing the motion' although all three shot prompts are filled. The message does not say the form field is the one that is empty. Filling the form prompt admits the sequence.
findings.harness_workaround: VID-03 types the form motion prompt as an operator would after reading the refusal.

evidence.description: VID-03 first run: the Queue Sequence refusal text

repair.summary: Sequence admission no longer demands the form-level motion prompt when every shot supplies its own (the form check is skipped for sequences only; experimental opt-in and accepted-control checks still run). A shot with no prompt of its own inherits the form prompt as before; an unprompted shot with a blank form prompt, or an explicitly empty prompt, is refused naming the shot. Each segment freezes its own prompt.

findings.title: A claimed job that waits for an unreachable backend is RUNNING with no 'preparing' state until the failure is classified
findings.area: Queue, executor readiness wait, WebUI outage coordinator
reproduction: Stop the WebUI endpoint, queue one job and let the runner claim it (OPS-01 case A).
Watch the queue label, the repository status and Operator Readiness for the first 30 to 120 seconds.
findings.expected: The operator can tell that a RUNNING job is waiting for the backend and that nothing has been dispatched.
findings.observed: The job is RUNNING (legitimately claimed) while the executor's readiness gate waits up to 120 s. The queue label says 'Running job...' and no hold exists until the failure is classified; then the job returns to the queue (typed no-dispatch evidence) and the hold applies. After GP832-F2 the readiness text names the claimed RUNNING job, but there is no in-flight signal from the executor.
findings.harness_workaround: None. OPS-01 accepts running or queued while down and asserts that whatever the banner says agrees with the job state.

evidence.description: OPS-01 unreachable_projection and unreachable_before_dispatch outcomes

repair.proposed_contract: Surface an in-flight 'waiting for the backend, nothing dispatched' signal from the executor through the runner to the queue projection, and decide whether the in-executor wait should reach the outage coordinator sooner so the hold applies earlier. This is new dispatch-certainty evidence and changes lifecycle semantics, so it needs owner approval.
repair.proposed_acceptance: A job claimed while the backend is unreachable shows 'waiting for the backend; nothing sent' within 5 s, never a hold it is not under, and still ends exactly once (requeued on typed no-dispatch evidence, otherwise failed).

findings.title: Opening a Storyboard asks 'Discard the unsaved draft changes?' after only the form was prepared
reproduction: Restart the application, choose a source image and a workflow, then Open Storyboard.
findings.expected: Opening a saved Storyboard replaces the form, so a prepared form is the only thing at stake.
findings.observed: A yes/no box 'Unsaved Storyboard - Discard the unsaved draft changes?' appears. The Storyboard draft includes the form inputs (source, workflow, settings), so a prepared form counts as an unsaved draft; the question is true and protects work.
findings.harness_workaround: The native dialog responder answers the question and then the file dialog (recorded as native_dialogs_N).

evidence.description: VID-03 Windows-driver native_dialogs observation

repair.classification: working as designed; no data-safety implication
repair.summary: Not a defect. Optional wording follow-up: say that opening replaces the current form and shots, and skip the question when the draft has no shots and no title.

findings.title: The Motion Library tree and the Review preview canvas capture the mouse wheel
findings.area: Video Workflow Motion Library; Review image preview
reproduction: Resize to the minimum window and open Video Workflow, Motion Library with several clips; scroll the page with the wheel over the list.
Open Review with an image loaded and scroll over the preview.
findings.expected: The wheel scrolls the page when the list or canvas has nothing more to scroll, or the page scrollbar stays easy to reach.
findings.observed: A list that fills the 262 px viewport (and the nested preview canvas) takes the wheel, so controls below it cannot be reached with the wheel; the page scrollbar still works.
findings.harness_workaround: The driver clicks the page scrollbar trough when the wheel stalls (scrolled_with_scrollbar, recorded as page_scrolled_with_the_scrollbar).

evidence.description: VID-02 minimum layout trace with scrolled_with_scrollbar

repair.proposed_acceptance: At 1280x680 every control in the Motion Library and Review tabs is reachable with the wheel alone; a layout test asserts wheel chaining to the page for nested lists and canvases.

findings.title: Review Edit Mask and Extend Canvas sit below the fold at the minimum window
reproduction: Resize to the minimum window, open Review and select an image.
findings.expected: The edit actions are visible, or reachable by wheel or scrollbar.
findings.observed: The actions are reachable by scrolling (the 760 reachability tests pass) but start out below the fold and the preview canvas captures the wheel (GP833-O2).
findings.harness_workaround: reach() scrolls the page, then clicks the scrollbar trough.

evidence.description: IMG-03 Windows-driver minimum layout trace

repair.proposed_acceptance: Primary Review actions are in an action bar visible without scrolling at 1280x680, or the declared minimum height is raised (owner decision, see the layout recommendation).

findings.harness_workaround: VID-03 expands Advanced options and Multi-shot sequence.

evidence.description: VID-03 journey opens the disclosures
